# Expert review packet {#packet}

**Purpose.** This is the list-review document promised after Expert Working Group 3.2 (August 13, 2026). Ben Wilder asked that the iconic species and special places lists circulate as products of the effort. Please mark keep / edit / remove, add missing items, and flag geographic gaps, especially **Sinaloa**.

**Return deadline: Tuesday, August 25, 2026, end of day (EOD).** Please send this Word file, or comments in the Google Sheets, by then.

**What this is not.** It is not a score-methods paper. Protection rules are summarized only so you know why a place is on a given list. Write method comments if you have them, but the main ask is: **are these the right species and places?**

**Companion document.** Feasibility responses to the EWG 3.2 Sense of Place discussion live in `ewg32_sp_postmeeting_responses_docx.qmd`.

**How to mark a row**

- **Keep:** the item belongs on the list as written.
- **Edit:** the item belongs, but the name, coordinates, region, or notes should change. Write the change in Comments.
- **Remove:** the item should not be treated as iconic / lasting special. Say why.
- **Add:** use the blank “Places or species to add” table under each section. Do not worry about perfect coordinates; a named place and region is enough.

# Iconic Species (ICO) {#ico}

## What this list is for

ICO scores the **risk status** of species that experts judged culturally iconic in the Gulf, not every harvested or habitat-forming species. For each region, the score is 100 times the mean risk weight of iconic species that occur there. Risk weights prefer NOM-059, then IUCN, then CITES. Special-case sheets override conflicts (for example Pacific versus Atlantic IUCN assessments).

**Inclusion reasons used when the list was built**

- Local ethnic or religious practices, including traditional fishing, hunting, or commerce that is place-based
- Existence value
- Locally recognized aesthetic value (tourism, art, whales, and similar)

Habitat-forming species and species harvested only for utilitarian commerce are outside this definition unless they also meet one of the reasons above.

Hector noted fish photography and iNaturalist patterns (including botete / pez globo) during EWG 3.2. If that should change the list, add or edit below.

# Lasting Special Places (LSP) {#lsp}

LSP scores **protection and management** of places the Expert Working Group named as lasting special places. There are six categories. A region’s LSP score is the unweighted mean of the categories that have features in that region.

**How condition is assigned, in brief**

| Category | Preferred condition | If that is missing |
|----------|---------------------|--------------------|
| Special protected areas | SIMEC i-efectividad | Ramsar management-plan status |
| Priority dive sites | SIMEC / Ramsar of overlapping PA | NOM-012-TUR floor, currently **58** |
| Iconic fishing sites | ZRP = 100; else TURF = 100 | SIMEC / Ramsar if in a PA |
| Archaeological sites | Nearby INAH match = 100 | Nearby PA SIMEC; else statute floor **30** |
| Special habitats | Better of PA score and statute floor | Mangrove / seagrass / coral floor **70**; coquina **30** |
| Other special places | SIMEC / Ramsar if inside a scored PA | Curated legal estimate (table later in this packet) |

Please review **membership of the lists** first. Floor values can be commented on at the end.

# Return instructions {#return}

Please return this Word file, or comments in the Google Sheets, to Sophia / the OHI Core Team.

**Deadline: Tuesday, August 25, 2026, end of day (EOD).**

**How comments will be used.** Additions and removals will be reviewed by the Core Team, then folded into the ICO and LSP inventories before the next score update. A place can be culturally important and still be deferred if we cannot assign a region or a protection pathway yet; those will be logged rather than silently dropped.
